China-nexus concept
China-nexus describes activity, infrastructure, or actors assessed to have some connection to China.
CI/CD pipelines concept
CI/CD pipelines are automated processes used to build, test, and deploy software changes.
cisa organization
CISA is the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which helps protect critical infrastructure and shares security guidance.
CISA BOD 23-01 other
CISA BOD 23-01 is a U.S. government directive that sets cybersecurity requirements for federal civilian agencies.
CISOs concept
CISOs are senior leaders responsible for an organization’s information security.
Citrix organization
Citrix is a company known for remote access, virtualization, and application delivery products.
Citrix Bleed One vulnerability
Citrix Bleed One is an informal name for a hacking campaign involving the exploitation of Citrix products.
Citrix NetScaler product
Citrix NetScaler is a product line for application delivery, load balancing, and secure remote access, now commonly branded as NetScaler.
Citrix NetScaler ADC product
Citrix NetScaler ADC is an application delivery controller used to manage, secure, and optimize access to applications.
Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway product
Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway is a product used to deliver applications and provide secure remote access to corporate systems.
Citrix NetScaler Gateway product
Citrix NetScaler Gateway is a remote-access gateway used to provide secure access to internal applications and networks.
Civil Penalties concept
Civil penalties are financial punishments ordered by a court or government agency for breaking a law or regulation.
claude
Claude is Anthropic’s family of AI assistants and language models.
Cleafy organization
Cleafy is a cybersecurity company that researches and helps detect financial fraud and malware.
clickfix
ClickFix is a social-engineering tactic that tricks users into copying and running malicious commands to “fix” a fake problem.
Client Secret concept
A client secret is a private value an application uses like a password to prove its identity to another service.
also: secret
client_id protocol
client_id is an identifier used in OAuth-style login flows to tell the identity provider which app is requesting access.
Clop threat-actor
Clop is a ransomware group and malware family known for stealing data and extorting victims.
CLOSEDQUORUM malware
CLOSEDQUORUM is a Windows malware family reported to use AI models to help choose and perform actions.
cloud concept
The cloud is internet-based computing where data and applications run on remote servers instead of only on your own device.
also: cloud data
Cloud credentials concept
Cloud credentials are passwords, keys, or tokens used to access cloud services and resources.
cloud environments concept
Cloud environments are computing systems and services run in cloud platforms rather than on local machines.
cloud infrastructure concept
Cloud infrastructure is computing infrastructure provided through internet-based services.
also: multi-cloud estate
Cloud misconfigurations concept
Incorrect cloud-service settings that can expose data, systems, or permissions.
Cloud Provider Ranges concept
Cloud provider ranges are blocks of internet addresses used by cloud-service providers.
Cloud Resource concept
A cloud resource is a computing service, such as a server, database, storage account, or application, hosted by a cloud provider.
cloud resources concept
Cloud resources are computing services like servers, storage, databases, or apps that run in an internet-hosted cloud environment.
cloud services concept
Computing resources—like storage, apps, and networking—delivered over the internet by providers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
cloud storage concept
Cloud storage is saving files on internet-based servers instead of only on a local device.
cloud-hosted concept
Stored or run on internet-connected provider infrastructure instead of directly on a local device.
Cloud-Storage Services concept
Online services that let people store, synchronize, and share files over the internet.
CNAME protocol
CNAME is a DNS record type that makes one domain name an alias for another domain name.
also: CNAME, MX, and NS records
code execution technique
Code execution means an attacker can make a computer or server run commands or software of their choosing.
Code repositories concept
Code repositories are storage locations where software source code and its change history are kept.
Cold Wallets concept
Cryptocurrency wallets kept offline, making them harder for online attackers to access.
also: offline cold wallets
command execution technique
Command execution means making a computer or device run instructions, often through a shell or remote interface.
command injection technique
Command injection is an attack where someone tricks an application into running system commands chosen by the attacker.
command injection flaw vulnerability
A security flaw that lets an attacker execute arbitrary commands on the host operating system through a vulnerable application.
command injection vulnerability vulnerability
A command injection vulnerability lets an attacker sneak operating-system commands into an application so the server runs them.
command server tool
A command server is an attacker-controlled system that sends instructions to malware or compromised devices.
command-and-control concept
Command-and-control is the way attackers remotely send instructions to malware and receive data back from infected machines.
also: C2 servers
Command-and-control domain concept
A command-and-control domain is an internet address malware uses to contact an attacker's server for instructions or to send stolen data.
Command-and-control server concept
Remote computers controlled by attackers that send orders to infected devices and collect stolen data.
Community Standards concept
Community Standards are rules that describe what content and behavior a platform says it will allow or remove.
COMPLETION concept
COMPLETION is a query or event label that generally refers to an autocomplete or completion action.
Composer tool
Composer is a dependency manager that helps PHP projects download and manage the libraries they need.
compromise concept
A compromise is a situation where a system, account, or data has been breached or taken over by an attacker.
compromised concept
Compromised means a system, account, or device has been accessed or controlled by someone who should not have access.
compromised accounts concept
Compromised accounts are user accounts that attackers have gained access to without permission.
compromised credentials concept
Compromised credentials are login details that have been stolen, exposed, or otherwise made unsafe.
also: stolen credentials, fresh and potentially valid credentials
compromised device concept
A phone, computer, or other device that an attacker has infected, accessed, or otherwise put at risk.
Compromised devices concept
Compromised devices are computers, phones, or systems that attackers have gained unauthorized control over.
compromised identity concept
A compromised identity is an account or digital identity that an attacker has taken control of or can use without permission.
Compromised maintainer accounts technique
Compromised maintainer accounts are trusted software publisher accounts that attackers have taken over to change or release malicious code.
Compromised Service Principals concept
Compromised service principals are stolen or misused cloud application identities that attackers can use to access resources.
also: compromised service principal
computer fraud concept
Computer fraud is the use of computers or online systems to deceive people or commit illegal acts.
computer networks concept
Computer networks are groups of connected devices that can share data with each other.
Confidential Phone Records concept
Private records containing information about phone customers, such as calls, account details, or billing data.
configuration changes concept
Configuration changes are modifications to settings that affect how a system, application, or device behaves.
Configuration drift concept
Configuration drift happens when systems slowly change from their intended settings over time, creating security or reliability risks.
also: drift
configuration files concept
Configuration files are files that store settings telling software or systems how to behave.
Connected Applications concept
Applications that have been linked to an account or service so they can access data or perform actions.
Connecting concept
Connecting is a status meaning a device, app, or service is trying to establish a network connection.
connector tool
A connector is software that links one system or service to another so they can exchange data or actions.
Connor Riley Moucka other
Connor Riley Moucka is a person named in security or law-enforcement reporting.
conspiracy concept
Conspiracy is an agreement between people to commit an unlawful act.
Contact Details concept
Information used to contact a person, such as an address, email address, or phone number.
Contact information concept
Contact information means details like an email address, phone number, or mailing address that can be used to reach someone.
containers concept
Containers are lightweight packages that run applications with their needed files in isolated environments.
containment technique
Containment is the process of limiting a cyber incident so attackers or malware cannot spread further.
Content hash concept
A content hash is a short digital fingerprint created from data so people can check whether the data changed.
Content Hashes concept
Short digital fingerprints calculated from a file's contents that help identify whether files are exactly the same.
Content moderation concept
Content moderation is the process of reviewing and removing or limiting posts, messages, or files that break rules or policies.
continuous concept
In security, continuous means something is monitored or updated all the time instead of only during occasional checks.
Continuous attack surface management concept
The ongoing process of finding and tracking internet-facing systems, services, and other possible entry points for attackers.
Continuous Identity Observability concept
Ongoing monitoring of how identities, such as users or AI agents, use access across systems.
continuous monitoring concept
Continuous monitoring means constantly watching systems, accounts, or networks for problems or suspicious activity.
also: monitoring continuously
continuous visibility concept
Continuous visibility means constantly monitoring systems and networks so defenders can see changes, weaknesses, and suspicious activity as they happen.
control panel product
A control panel is an interface used to manage settings, accounts, systems, or services.
coordination concept
Coordination is the organized sharing of tasks, information, and decisions among people or teams.
CoreGraphics product
An Apple software framework that applications use to draw graphics and handle visual content.
Corelight organization
Corelight is a cybersecurity company that provides network detection and response products.
Corporate Directories concept
Corporate directories are company lists of employees, roles, contact details, and organizational information.
also: directory data, employee datasets, employee or directory information, corporate directory information
Corporate Directory concept
A corporate directory is an organization's list of employees, accounts, groups, roles, and contact information.
correlation concept
Correlation means finding connections between separate events, data points, or alerts that may be related.
Correlations tool
A security feature that links related alerts, events, or findings to help analysts investigate them together.
Cortex Xpanse tool
Cortex Xpanse is a Palo Alto Networks tool that discovers and monitors an organization’s internet-exposed systems.
Covert concept
Kept secret so that others do not know an activity is taking place or who is doing it.
crafted file technique
A crafted file is a specially made file designed to trigger a bug, exploit a weakness, or test how software handles unusual input.
credential concept
A credential is proof of identity for logging in, such as a password, security token, API key, or certificate.
credential collection technique
The process of harvesting usernames, passwords, and tokens, typically by malware or phishing, to gain unauthorized access.
also: harvested credentials, credential collection-related operations
Credential Spraying technique
An attack that tries a few common passwords against many accounts to avoid triggering login protections.
credential theft technique
Credential theft is the stealing of usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login information.
credential-phishing
Credential phishing is a scam that tricks people into entering usernames, passwords, or codes into a fake login page.
credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.
Credit Card Data concept
Information from payment cards that can be used to process transactions or commit fraud if stolen.
Credit Card Information concept
Credit card information includes card numbers and related details that can be used to make payments.
criminal forums concept
Online discussion sites where criminals may trade stolen data, access to hacked systems, or attack services.
Critical backend system concept
An essential server-side system whose failure or compromise can seriously affect a service's operations or security.
CRM concept
CRM stands for customer relationship management, which refers to systems and data used to manage sales and customer interactions.
cron jobs tool
Cron jobs are scheduled tasks on Unix-like systems that automatically run commands at set times.
Cross-Chain Swap Services concept
Cross-chain swap services let users exchange digital assets between different blockchain networks.
cryptocurrency concept
Cryptocurrency is digital money, such as Bitcoin, that uses cryptography and usually runs on a blockchain.
Cryptocurrency exchange concept
An online service where people can buy, sell, trade, or store digital currencies.
cryptocurrency wallet product
A cryptocurrency wallet is software or hardware used to store and use the keys that control digital coins.
cryptocurrency wallets product
Cryptocurrency wallets are tools used to store and manage access to digital currency funds.
CTX697096 other
CTX697096 is a Citrix security bulletin that provides information and fixes for NetScaler vulnerabilities.
curl
curl is a command-line tool used to transfer data to or from servers using protocols like HTTP and HTTPS.
customer data concept
Customer data is information a company keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, or purchase history.
customer information concept
Customer information is data a business keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, purchases, or account records.
Customer Records concept
Stored information about customers, such as names, account details, and contact information.
customer-facing services concept
Customer-facing services are websites, apps, or systems that customers can directly use.
CVE vulnerability
A CVE is a public identifier used to track a specific known software vulnerability.
CVE Numbering Authority organization
A CVE Numbering Authority is an organization authorized to assign CVE identifiers to publicly known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVEs concept
CVEs are standardized public identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVSS 10.0 concept
CVSS 10.0 is the highest severity score on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System scale for rating security flaws.
also: maximum-severity
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
CVSS v4.0 concept
CVSS v4.0 is version 4.0 of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, a standard way to rate how serious a vulnerability is.
cyber concept
Cyber is a broad shorthand for things related to computers, networks, and digital security.
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
cyber threats concept
Cyber threats are possible dangers to computers, networks, or data caused by attackers or malicious software.
cyberattack concept
A cyberattack is an attempt to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.
Cybercrime forums concept
Cybercrime forums are online communities where criminals trade stolen data, malware, services, and advice.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
Cyble organization
Cyble is a cybersecurity company that provides threat intelligence and digital risk monitoring.
Cyble Attack Surface Management product
Cyble Attack Surface Management is a security product for discovering and monitoring an organization's internet-exposed systems.
Cyble ODIN product
Cyble ODIN is Cyble's platform for cyber intelligence, exposure monitoring, and attack-surface visibility.
also: Odin
Cyera organization
Cyera is a cybersecurity company focused on discovering and protecting sensitive data across cloud and enterprise systems.
Cyera Research organization
Cyera Research is the security research team associated with the data security company Cyera.
DAEMON Tools Lite tool
A legitimate Windows application for mounting disk-image files as virtual drives.
Danglegeddon concept
Danglegeddon is a named security issue or campaign term related to large-scale dangling-DNS and takeover risks.
dangling CNAME vulnerability
A dangling CNAME is a DNS alias that still points to a service or domain that is no longer controlled, which can let attackers take it over.
Dangling CNAME Records concept
Dangling CNAME records are DNS aliases that still point to a service that no longer exists and may be claimable by someone else.
Dangling DNS concept
Dangling DNS happens when a domain name still points to a cloud or web resource that no longer exists and could be claimed by someone else.
Dangling DNS Record concept
A dangling DNS record is an old domain record that points to a deleted service and can sometimes be abused to take over a subdomain.
dangling DNS records concept
Dangling DNS records are domain settings that still point to a service or resource that no longer exists or is no longer controlled by the domain owner.
Dangling MX Records concept
Dangling MX records are email-routing DNS records that still point to mail services that are no longer under the owner's control.
Dangling NS Records concept
Dangling NS records are DNS delegation records that point to name servers no longer controlled by the domain owner.
Dark web concept
The dark web is a part of the internet that requires special tools to access and is often discussed in relation to hidden marketplaces and forums.
Data access concept
Data access means the ability to view, use, change, or retrieve information from a system.
Data Boundaries concept
Limits that define what information a user, program, or AI agent is allowed to access or use.
data breaches concept
Data breaches happen when private or sensitive information is exposed, stolen, or accessed without permission.
data exposure concept
Data exposure means sensitive information is left accessible to people or systems that should not be able to see it.
data leak site tool
A data leak site is a website used to publish or threaten publication of stolen information.
data lineage concept
Data lineage shows where data came from, how it changed, and where it moved over time.
Data Lineage Graph concept
A visual map showing where data or files came from and how they moved or changed over time.
Data owners concept
Data owners are people responsible for deciding how particular organizational data should be used, protected, and shared.
data privacy concept
The right and practice of protecting personal and sensitive information from unauthorized access, collection, or exposure.
Data Privacy Practices concept
Data privacy practices are the rules and actions an organization uses to collect, use, store, and share personal information.
Data protection concept
Data protection means keeping information safe from loss, theft, exposure, or unauthorized changes.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
data-theft-extortion technique
Data-theft-extortion is when criminals steal information and threaten to publish or sell it unless the victim pays.
also: stealing data and threatening to release it on a data leak site unless the victim pays a ransom, extortion communications
Database Connection Strings concept
Settings that tell an application how to connect to a database, sometimes including sensitive login details.
Database logs concept
Database logs are records of database activity such as queries, logins, errors, and changes.
Database Permissions concept
Database permissions are rules that determine who can view, change, or manage data in a database.
DataBreaches organization
A news and information website focused on data breaches and privacy incidents.
Datagram Transport Layer Security protocol
Datagram Transport Layer Security, or DTLS, is a protocol that encrypts and protects data sent over connectionless networks such as UDP.
Decommissioned Cloud Resource concept
A decommissioned cloud resource is a cloud service that has been shut down or removed.
Decrypt technique
Decrypt is a cryptographic operation that turns encrypted data back into readable data when the correct key is used.
decryption concept
Decryption is the process of turning scrambled encrypted data back into readable information.
defaced technique
Defaced means a website has been altered without permission, often to show an attacker’s message.
defacement technique
Defacement is when an attacker changes a website or screen to show unauthorized content.
Default configurations concept
Default configurations are factory or out-of-the-box settings that may be unsafe if not changed.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
denial-of-service
Denial-of-service is an attack that overwhelms a system so legitimate users cannot access it.
Deprovisioning Services technique
Deprovisioning services means shutting down and removing services that are no longer needed.
also: service is switched off, services are deprovisioned
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detection guidance concept
Detection guidance is advice that helps defenders find signs of suspicious or malicious activity in their systems.
detection rules concept
Detection rules are instructions security tools use to flag suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.
detections concept
Alerts or findings generated by security tools indicating that a potential threat or malicious activity has been identified.
device_code protocol
device_code is a code used behind the scenes in OAuth device login to identify the device waiting for user approval.
digital assets concept
Digital assets are valuable items that exist electronically, such as cryptocurrency, tokens, files, or online accounts.
digital currency concept
Digital currency is money or value that exists electronically rather than as physical cash.
Directory Enumeration technique
Directory enumeration is the process of listing users, groups, computers, or other information from an organization's identity directory.
Directory-Enumeration Behavior technique
Directory-enumeration behavior is the searching, listing, or exporting of many user and organization records from an identity directory.
also: bulk user enumeration, directory exports, directory export
Directory-Read Permissions concept
Directory-read permissions allow a person or application to view information stored in an organization's identity directory.
also: directory-reading permissions, directory-read access
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
Disclosure Timeline concept
A disclosure timeline is a planned schedule for reporting, fixing, and publicly sharing information about a security flaw.
Discovery technique
Discovery is the attacker activity of learning about a victim’s systems, accounts, and network before taking further action.
disruption concept
Disruption is an interruption that prevents systems, services, or operations from working normally.
DKIM protocol
DKIM is an email signing method that helps verify that a message was authorized by a domain and was not changed after signing.
DLL concept
A DLL is a Windows file that contains code other programs can load and use.
DLL sideloading technique
DLL sideloading is an attack where malware places a fake DLL where a trusted Windows program will load it.
DMARC protocol
DMARC is an email policy check that uses SPF or DKIM alignment to help determine whether a message claiming to come from a domain should be trusted.
DNS protocol
DNS is the internet system that turns human-readable names like example.com into the numeric addresses computers use to find websites and services.
DNS Record protocol
A DNS record is an entry that tells the internet how to find or handle a domain name, such as its IP address or mail server.
also: record, records
DNS records protocol
DNS records are internet directory entries that connect domain names with technical information such as addresses.
DNS zone protocol
A DNS zone is the portion of the domain name system managed as one administrative unit, such as all records for a domain.
docker
Docker is a platform for packaging and running applications in containers.
Docker Daemons product
Docker daemons are background services that create and manage Docker containers on a computer.
double extortion attacks technique
Ransomware attacks in which criminals both encrypt systems and threaten to publish stolen data unless paid.
also: double-extortion
downtime concept
Downtime is a period when a system, website, or service is unavailable or not working.
dragonforce
DragonForce is a ransomware group that extorts victims by stealing data and encrypting systems.
Driver’s license concept
A driver’s license is a government-issued card that proves someone is allowed to drive and is often used to confirm identity.
Driver’s License Information concept
Personal information and images contained on a person's driver's license.
driver’s licenses concept
Driver’s licenses are government-issued identity documents that can be valuable to criminals if stolen or exposed.
Drydock tool
Drydock is a software supply-chain security tool that helps maintainers inspect software releases before approving them.
DTLS protocol
DTLS is a security protocol that protects datagram network traffic, similar to how TLS protects web connections.
Dutch authorities organization
Dutch authorities are government agencies or officials from the Netherlands.
Dutch government organization
The Dutch government is the national government of the Netherlands.
Dutch National Cyber Security Center organization
The Dutch National Cyber Security Center is the Netherlands government body that provides cybersecurity advice, warnings, and incident support.
Dutch police organization
Dutch police are the law-enforcement authorities of the Netherlands.
EDR product
EDR is security software that monitors computers and servers for suspicious activity and helps respond to attacks.
also: endpoint detection and response (EDR)
elastic organization
The company behind Elasticsearch and the Elastic Stack, providing search, observability, and security solutions.
Elastic Agent Builder tool
A tool from Elastic that helps administrators build customized, single-package agents for deploying security monitoring software.
also: Agent Builder
Elastic Defend product
Elastic Defend is Elastic’s endpoint security product for detecting, preventing, and investigating threats on computers and servers.
also: native EDR
Elastic Security product
Elastic Security is Elastic’s security analytics platform for SIEM, endpoint protection, and threat detection.
Elastic Security Labs organization
Elastic Security Labs is the threat research team at Elastic that studies attacks, malware, and security trends.
Elastic Workflows product
Automated sequences of actions within Elastic's security platform that help analysts investigate and respond to threats.
electronic devices concept
Electronic devices are powered gadgets such as phones, computers, tablets, or other hardware that can store or process data.
ElevenLabs organization
ElevenLabs is an AI company known for services that generate realistic synthetic speech and voices.
Elliptic organization
Elliptic is a company that analyzes cryptocurrency transactions to help detect fraud, sanctions evasion, and money laundering.
email accounts concept
Email accounts are user accounts that let people send, receive, and store email messages.
email address concept
An email address is the unique address used to send messages to someone's email account.
email addresses concept
Email addresses are the unique names people use to send and receive email, such as user@example.com.
EncForge tool
EncForge is a named tool or malware family referenced in security reporting, likely associated with encryption-related activity.
also: compiled Go-based ransomware strain
encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.
encrypted archive concept
An encrypted archive is a compressed file, such as a ZIP or RAR, protected so its contents cannot be read without a key or password.
Encryption keys concept
Encryption keys are secret values used to lock and unlock protected data.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
also: The endpoint, endpoints, host
Endpoint Events concept
Records of actions that happen on a device, such as opening, changing, copying, or deleting a file.
endpoint telemetry concept
Endpoint telemetry is activity data collected from computers, servers, or mobile devices to help detect and investigate security issues.
ENISA organization
ENISA is the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, which supports cybersecurity policy, guidance, and coordination across Europe.
enrichment technique
Enrichment adds extra context to raw security data, such as looking up an IP address, domain, or account to make it more useful.
enterprise applications product
Enterprise applications are software systems used by organizations to run business functions such as HR, finance, sales, or operations.
Enterprise networks concept
Enterprise networks are the large computer networks used by businesses, governments, or other organizations.
enterprise systems product
Enterprise systems are large business technology systems used to run important organizational operations.
entitlements concept
Entitlements are permissions or access rights that say what a user, app, or device is allowed to do.
Entra product
Microsoft Entra is Microsoft’s identity and access management product family, including cloud directory and login services.
enumerate technique
To enumerate means to systematically list or discover items such as users, devices, services, or files during security testing.
Enumeration technique
Enumeration is the process of systematically listing users, files, services, or other details about a system.
Ephemeral Assets concept
Ephemeral assets are short-lived computing resources that are created and removed quickly, often in cloud environments.
eth concept
The standard network interface naming prefix for Ethernet devices in Linux and Unix-like systems.
ethereum
Ethereum is a blockchain platform used for cryptocurrency, smart contracts, and decentralized applications.
european-union
The European Union is a political and economic union of European countries that also creates cybersecurity and privacy rules.
EvilTokens tool
EvilTokens is a named tool or technique referenced in security reporting for abusing or stealing authentication tokens.
EVM Networks protocol
EVM networks are blockchains compatible with the Ethereum Virtual Machine, allowing Ethereum-style smart contracts to run on them.
Exceptions concept
Exceptions are errors or unusual conditions that software handles while running.
excessive access concept
Excessive access means a person or account has more permissions than they actually need, increasing security risk.
excessive permissions vulnerability
Excessive permissions are access rights that are broader than a person, app, or token actually needs.
executable concept
An executable is a file that can run as a program on a computer.
Execution technique
Execution is the stage where an attacker runs code or commands on a target system.
executive impersonation technique
Executive impersonation is when a scammer pretends to be a company leader to trick people into sending money, sharing information, or taking risky actions.
exploit technique
An exploit is code or a method that takes advantage of a security flaw to make something happen that should not be allowed.
Exploitability concept
Exploitability describes how easily an attacker can take advantage of a security weakness.
exploitation technique
Exploitation is taking advantage of a weakness in software or people to gain unauthorized access or control.
exploitation attempts technique
Exploitation attempts are tries to take advantage of a software weakness to gain access, run code, or cause harm.
Exploited technique
Exploited means attackers successfully took advantage of a weakness in software or a system.
exploited in the wild concept
Exploited in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just in a lab.
Exposed concept
Accessible in a way that could allow a threat to reach or affect a system.
Exposed services concept
Network-connected systems or applications that are reachable by people or devices outside the organization.
external attack surface concept
An external attack surface is everything an organization exposes to the internet that attackers could try to target.
also: external footprint
External domains concept
External domains are internet addresses outside an organization's own network that systems may connect to.
Extort concept
To extort someone means to pressure or threaten them into paying money or doing something.
Extorting concept
Extorting means threatening someone to force them to pay money or do something.
Extorting victims technique
Extorting victims means threatening people or organizations to force them to pay money or meet demands.
extortion concept
Extortion is pressuring someone to give up money, data, or something valuable through threats.
extortion demands concept
Extortion demands are threats from attackers asking for money or concessions to avoid harm or data release.
extortion operation technique
An extortion operation is an attack in which criminals threaten to expose, damage, or withhold access to data unless they are paid.
f5
F5 is a company that provides application delivery, load balancing, web security, and NGINX products.
F5 BIG-IP product
F5 BIG-IP is a networking product commonly used to manage application traffic, load balancing, and security.
F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager product
F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager is an F5 product that manages secure user access to applications, VPNs, and networks.
Facebook product
Facebook is a major social networking platform operated by Meta.
Fake Login Page technique
A fraudulent webpage made to look like a real sign-in page so attackers can steal credentials.
Fake Login Screens technique
Fake login screens are imitation sign-in pages used to trick people into entering their passwords or other credentials.
fbi organization
The FBI is the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation, which investigates cybercrime and national security threats.
FBI Jobs Site organization
The Federal Bureau of Investigation website used to advertise and manage job opportunities.
also: a jobs website run by the agency
FBIjobs.gov organization
The official United States Federal Bureau of Investigation job application website.
federal agencies organization
Federal agencies are government organizations that operate at the national level.
Federal Bureau of Investigation organization
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is the main U.S. federal law-enforcement agency that investigates crimes including cybercrime.
also: the agency, F.B.I.
federal civilian agencies organization
Government organizations that provide public services rather than military functions.
Federal Civilian Executive Branch organization
Federal Civilian Executive Branch refers to U.S. federal civilian agencies that are part of the executive branch.
also: FCEB
Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies organization
Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies are U.S. federal agencies outside the military and intelligence communities that run civilian government functions.
fiat concept
Fiat money is government-issued currency such as dollars or euros, as opposed to cryptocurrency or other virtual assets.
file creation technique
File creation is the act of making a new file on a computer or server, which can matter in security if attackers create files to gain control or hide activity.
File Family concept
A group of related copies or versions of the same file.

Okta is a company that provides identity and login management services for organizations.
On-Chain Tracing technique
The process of following cryptocurrency transfers through the public records stored on a blockchain.
On-demand webinar concept
An on-demand webinar is a recorded online presentation that people can watch whenever they choose.
online platforms concept
Online platforms are websites or apps where people can post, share, or communicate with others.
Online Safety concept
Online Safety refers to policies and practices intended to reduce harm, abuse, fraud, and other risks on the internet.
online services concept
Online services are websites, apps, or internet-based systems that provide functions to users over the internet.
Open ports concept
Network connection points that are accepting traffic and may expose services to the internet.
open source concept
Open source means software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, modify, and share.
Open source software concept
Open source software is software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, and improve.
Open-Source AI Agents concept
Open-source AI agents are AI-driven programs whose source code is publicly available and that can perform tasks with limited supervision.
openai organization
OpenAI is an AI company known for ChatGPT and GPT language models.
also: OpenAI models
OpenAI Agent product
An AI-based software agent made by OpenAI that can carry out tasks such as searching for information or using online services.
also: agent
OpenJS organization
OpenJS is an organization that supports JavaScript open-source projects and communities.
OpenJS Foundation organization
The OpenJS Foundation is an organization that supports JavaScript projects such as Node.js and helps coordinate their governance and security processes.
Operating system concept
An operating system is the main software that manages a computer or phone, such as Windows, macOS, Android, or iOS.
also: an operating system, the underlying operating system
Operator tool
An Operator is a Kubernetes automation component that manages an application by encoding operational tasks into software.
operator console tool
A control panel used by an administrator or operator to manage a service or campaign.
operators concept
Operators are the people or groups running a system, service, campaign, or criminal operation.
Optimism product
A blockchain network designed to process Ethereum-related transactions more cheaply and quickly.
oracle
Oracle is a technology company known for databases, enterprise software, cloud services, and Java-related products.
Oracle PeopleSoft product
Oracle PeopleSoft is a suite of enterprise applications used for business functions such as HR, finance, and administration.
also: Oracle’s PeopleSoft
Orchid Security organization
A cybersecurity company specializing in identity security and cloud infrastructure entitlement management.
Organizing concept
The act of planning, arranging, or coordinating an activity or group.
OTP Service concept
A service that sends or checks one-time passwords, often by text message, for login verification.

A memory corruption vulnerability where a program writes data outside the allocated memory buffer, often leading to code execution.
Out-of-bounds write flaw vulnerability
An out-of-bounds write flaw is a memory bug where software writes data outside the area it was supposed to use.
outbound connections concept
Outbound connections are network connections that start from inside a system or network and go out to another destination.
Outdated concept
Outdated means software, data, or settings are old and may be missing important fixes or protections.
Outside-In Discovery technique
Outside-in discovery finds an organization's internet-facing systems from an external attacker's point of view.
oversight concept
Oversight means watching over an activity or organization to make sure rules are followed and problems are caught.
OWASP organization
OWASP is a nonprofit security organization best known for publishing widely used guidance on web application risks.
pace concept
Pace is the speed or rhythm of speech, movement, or activity and can be used as a behavior signal.
Packagist product
Packagist is the main public package repository used by Composer for PHP software libraries.
Palo Alto Networks organization
A leading global cybersecurity company known for next-generation firewalls and advanced cloud security.
PamStealer malware
PamStealer is a malware family referenced in security reporting that is designed to steal information from infected systems.
Panda Workshop V5 tool
Panda Workshop V5 is a named version of a RatHat operator console used to manage malware activity.
Panda Workshop V6 tool
Panda Workshop V6 is a named version of a RatHat operator console used to manage malware activity.
Park24 Group organization
A Japanese corporate group that operates parking and mobility-related businesses.
password hashes concept
Password hashes are scrambled versions of passwords that systems store so they do not have to keep the plain passwords.
password reset concept
The process of changing a user's password, typically after they've forgotten it or it's been compromised.
patch concept
A patch is an update that fixes a software bug or security problem.
also: a patch, the patch, Oracle’s June security update
patched concept
Patched means a software flaw has been fixed with an update.
patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept
Applying software updates to fix security holes and bugs.
Patient Records concept
Documents and data containing an individual's medical history, treatment, and healthcare information.
payload concept
A payload is the part of malicious code that performs the attacker’s intended action.
payment card product
A payment card is a credit, debit, or similar card used to pay for goods and services.
Payment card information concept
Payment card information is data from credit or debit cards, such as card numbers, names, expiration dates, or security codes.
Payment details concept
Payment details are information used to pay for something, such as card numbers, billing addresses, or bank account data.
Payment systems concept
Payment systems are the services and networks that let people and businesses send, receive, and process money.
Payroll concept
Records and processes used by an organization to pay its workers.
PDF attachment concept
A PDF attachment is a PDF file included with an email or message, sometimes used by attackers to deliver scams or malware links.
PDF attachments concept
PDF attachments are PDF files sent with messages, and attackers often use them to deliver scams, links, or malware.
PeopleSoft product
PeopleSoft is Oracle enterprise software used for business functions such as human resources, finance, and administration.
PeopleSoft Configuration Files concept
Files containing settings that control how Oracle PeopleSoft software connects to services and operates.
Perl product
Perl is a programming language commonly used for scripting and text processing.
Perl Script concept
A Perl script is a small program written in the Perl programming language.
persistence concept
Persistence is the ability for an attacker to keep access to a system over time.
persistent access concept
Persistent access means continued access to an account or system over time.
Persistent remote access technique
Persistent remote access means an attacker keeps a way to reconnect to a system even after reboots or temporary disruptions.
personal cloud storage concept
Personal cloud storage is internet-based storage controlled by an individual rather than centrally by an organization.
personal data concept
Information relating to an identifiable individual, such as name, email, location, or financial details.
personal details concept
Personal details are information about a person, such as their name, address, phone number, or financial data, that can be misused if stolen.
personal information concept
Personal information is data that can identify or describe a person, such as a name, address, phone number, or account details.
personally identifiable information concept
Personally identifiable information is data that can identify a person, such as a name, address, Social Security number, or email address.
PESEL concept
PESEL is Poland's national personal identification number assigned to residents.
Pharmaceutical concept
Pharmaceutical refers to organizations that research, make, or distribute medicines.
philippines other
The Philippines is a country in Southeast Asia that may be mentioned in cyber reports as a victim location, actor location, or operating base.
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.
also: phishing emails, phishing quarantine
phishing attacks technique
Deceptive emails or messages that trick recipients into revealing personal information or installing malware.
also: internal phishing messages
phishing campaign technique
A phishing campaign is a coordinated effort to trick people into giving up passwords, money, or other sensitive information.
phishing campaigns technique
Phishing campaigns are organized attempts to trick many people into revealing information or installing malware using fake messages.
phishing email technique
A phishing email is a fake or deceptive message designed to trick someone into revealing information or clicking something harmful.
Phishing lure technique
A phishing lure is the fake message, link, or story used to trick someone into clicking or sharing information.
Phishing page technique
A phishing page is a fake web page designed to trick people into entering passwords, payment details, or other sensitive information.
Phishing-resistant authentication concept
Phishing-resistant authentication is a login method designed so fake websites cannot easily steal or reuse the user’s credentials.
phone calls protocol
Phone calls are voice conversations made over telephone networks or internet calling services.
Phone number concept
A phone number is a personal contact detail that attackers may steal or misuse for scams and account recovery attacks.
phone numbers concept
Phone numbers are the unique numbers used to reach people or devices on telephone networks.
PII concept
PII means personally identifiable information, such as names, addresses, ID numbers, or other data that can identify a person.
pivot technique
A pivot is an investigative move where one clue is used to find another related clue, such as moving from a domain to linked IP addresses.
plaintext concept
Plaintext is information stored or sent in a readable, unprotected form.
plaintext passwords concept
Plaintext passwords are passwords stored or shown in readable form rather than hidden or transformed.
Poedit product
A legitimate software application used to edit translation files.
Point-in-Time Scan technique
A point-in-time scan is a one-time security check that shows a system's condition only at the moment it runs.
also: point-in-time scanning, periodic snapshots
Pokémon other
A popular Japanese media and video-game franchise about fictional creatures called Pokémon.
poland other
Poland is a country in Europe.
Polish Data Protection Authority organization
The Polish Data Protection Authority is Poland's government regulator responsible for enforcing privacy and data protection rules.
politicians other
Politicians are people who hold or seek government office and may be targeted in cyber stories because of their influence or access to sensitive information.
port 2375 protocol
A network port commonly used for an unencrypted Docker management interface, which can be dangerous if exposed without access controls.
Post-compromise activity technique
Post-compromise activity is what attackers do after they have already broken into a system.
Post-compromise operations concept
Post-compromise operations are the actions attackers take after they have already broken into a system, such as stealing data or moving deeper into a network.
PostgreSQL product
PostgreSQL is a database system used to store and manage data.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.
also: PowerShell command, PowerShell process
pre-authentication concept
Pre-authentication means something happens before a user has logged in or proven who they are.
Pre-Authentication Command Injection technique
Pre-authentication command injection is a flaw that lets an attacker make a system run commands before logging in.
Pre-Authentication Request concept
A pre-authentication request is a request sent to a service before a user has logged in.
also: pre-authentication login request
Preemptive Cyber Defense concept
Preemptive cyber defense means taking protective action before an attack succeeds or even before it begins.
also: Preemptive Cyber Defense team
Prioritization concept
Prioritization means deciding which issues or tasks should be handled first based on importance or risk.
private data concept
Sensitive information that should not be publicly disclosed, like personal identifiers or financial records.
private keys concept
Private keys are secret cryptographic values used to prove identity, decrypt data, or authorize cryptocurrency transactions.
private messages concept
Private messages are direct messages meant to be visible only to selected users.
Private repositories concept
Private repositories are online code storage spaces visible only to approved users.
private sector organization
The private sector is the part of the economy made up of businesses and organizations not run by the government.
Private security companies organization
Private security companies are businesses that provide security services outside of government law enforcement or military forces.
Privileged accounts concept
Privileged accounts are user or service accounts with powerful permissions that can make major changes to systems or data.
privileged container concept
A software container given unusually broad access to the underlying computer, making it risky if compromised.
Privileged containers concept
Privileged containers are software containers given elevated access to the host system, which can be risky if abused.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
PromptSpy tool
PromptSpy is a named cyber tool, malware, or technique label referenced in security reporting.
Protection Fund product
A reserve of money set aside by a platform to help cover losses from certain incidents or emergencies.
Proven Lineage concept
A confirmed history of how a file moved, changed, or was copied, supported by sufficient evidence.
Public Keys concept
Public keys are shareable cryptographic values used to verify identities or encrypt information without revealing a secret private key.
Qbusoft organization
Qbusoft is a Polish healthcare software provider.
Qilin threat-actor
A ransomware threat-actor group known for providing and using malware to extort victims.
qilin
Qilin is a ransomware group that steals data and encrypts victim systems for extortion.
QR concept
QR usually refers to a QR code, a square barcode that phones can scan to open links or store information.
Qt tool
Qt is a software development framework used to build graphical applications across different operating systems.
quarantine technique
Quarantine is a holding area where suspicious files or emails are isolated so they cannot cause harm right away.
also: quarantines, blast-radius quarantine
quarantined concept
Quarantined means a suspicious file, email, or system has been isolated so it cannot easily cause harm while it is investigated.
Queries concept
Requests sent to a database to retrieve, add, change, or remove information.
also: any queries, database activity
Railway product
Railway is a cloud hosting platform used to deploy applications and services.
ransom demands concept
Ransom demands are requests from criminals for payment, usually in exchange for restoring access to stolen or encrypted data.
ransom note concept
A ransom note is a message telling a victim that files have been locked or data stolen and giving payment or contact instructions.
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
also: ransomware operation, ransomware-aligned
ransomware activity concept
Ransomware activity is behavior related to malware that locks or steals data and demands payment from victims.
ransomware attack concept
A ransomware attack is when criminals lock files or systems and demand payment to restore access or prevent data leaks.
Ransomware deployment technique
Ransomware deployment is the stage where attackers install or run ransomware on victim systems.
ransomware gangs threat-actor
Criminal groups that use malicious software to encrypt victims' data and demand payment for its release.
ransomware group threat-actor
A ransomware group is a criminal or threat-actor team that uses malware to lock or steal data and demand payment.
ransomware operators threat-actor
Ransomware operators are criminals who run attacks that lock or steal data and demand payment from victims.
RatHat malware
An Android malware family that can remotely control infected phones and steal sensitive information.
Raw logs concept
Raw logs are the original event records produced by systems before they are filtered, summarized, or analyzed.
RCE vulnerability
RCE, or remote code execution, is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands or programs on someone else's system from afar.
Readable Tables concept
Database tables whose contents can be viewed by a user or system.
recommendation concept
A recommendation is suggested guidance or an action that someone should consider taking to reduce risk or solve a problem.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
also: enumeration activity, resource discovery, discovery operation
Recover concept
Recover is a cybersecurity function focused on restoring systems, data, and services after an incident.
Recovery Protection Locks concept
Recovery protection locks are safeguards intended to stop attackers or administrators from deleting backup and recovery resources.
Regional CSO concept
A Regional CSO is a regional chief security officer responsible for security leadership in a particular geographic area.
relay concept
A relay is a server or service that forwards network traffic or email from one place to another.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
remote attackers concept
Remote attackers are people who try to affect a system over a network rather than by physically accessing it.

A remote code execution vulnerability is a flaw that can let an attacker run commands on a system from afar.
also: execute code over the network
remote command execution vulnerability
Remote command execution is when an attacker can run operating-system commands on another computer over a network.
remote control technique
Remote control means operating a computer, phone, or system from another location over a network.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
Remote-code-execution flaws vulnerability
Remote-code-execution flaws are vulnerabilities that can let an attacker run commands on a system from afar.
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
Replayed technique
Replayed means captured data, such as a token or request, is sent again to try to repeat an action or gain access.
Replit product
An online development platform for writing, running, and sharing code, including AI-assisted development tools.
repositories concept
Repositories are places where software project files and related development data are stored.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
resource locks concept
Resource locks are cloud settings that help prevent important resources from being accidentally or maliciously deleted or changed.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
restitution concept
Restitution is money a court orders a defendant to pay back to victims for losses caused by a crime.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
reverse SSH tunnel technique
A reverse SSH tunnel is a connection that lets someone reach a machine behind a firewall by having that machine first connect outward to another server.
Reverse Tunnel technique
A network connection created from inside a private network to an outside server, allowing external access back into the private system.
revocation concept
The process of invalidating a digital credential or certificate so it can no longer be used.
RFC 8693 protocol
An Internet standard defining OAuth 2.0 token exchange, which allows one access token to be exchanged for another.
risk management concept
Risk management is the process of identifying, reducing, and preparing for things that could go wrong.
Risk-Control Threshold concept
A risk-control threshold is a set limit that causes a system to flag, block, or review activity considered risky.
also: risk controls, Bitget's risk-control threshold
Rogue Agents concept
Rogue agents are automated AI agents that act without proper approval, control, or safe limits.
Row-Level Security technique
A database feature that restricts which individual rows of data each user is allowed to see or change.
run code concept
To run code means to make a computer execute instructions written in a programming language.
runtime concept
Runtime is the period when a program is actively running, or the software environment it needs in order to run.
Runtime behavior concept
Runtime behavior is what software actually does while it is running, such as files it opens or network connections it makes.
Runtime Telemetry concept
Data collected about what software does while it is running, such as actions, errors, and resource use.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
SaaS concept
SaaS is software delivered over the internet as a subscription or hosted service instead of installed and managed entirely by the customer.
SaaS applications concept
SaaS applications are software services delivered over the internet rather than installed and managed locally by each organization.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
sailpoint
SailPoint is an identity security company that helps organizations manage who has access to systems and data.
Santander organization
Santander is a major international bank headquartered in Spain.
Saviynt organization
A cybersecurity company that provides identity governance and cloud access-management products.
Scam technique
A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
scam pages technique
Web pages made to deceive visitors into giving money, passwords, or personal information.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.

Scattered Spider is a cybercrime group known for social engineering, account theft, and high-profile intrusions.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
screen-capture technique
Screen capture is the act of taking an image or recording of what is shown on a device's screen.
also: app's own screen capture
screencap tool
screencap is an Android command or tool used to take a screenshot of a device screen.
Securing AI concept
Securing AI means protecting artificial intelligence systems from misuse, manipulation, data leaks, and unsafe behavior.
Security alerts concept
Security alerts are warnings from tools or services that something suspicious or risky may be happening.
security checks technique
Security checks are tests or reviews used to find risks, weaknesses, or unsafe behavior in a system.
Security Gateway product
A Security Gateway is a device or service that inspects and controls network traffic to enforce security rules.
Security Group concept
A security group is a set of network access rules that controls which traffic can reach a cloud resource.
Security Management concept
Security Management is the process or product area for configuring, monitoring, and enforcing security controls.
also: Security Management products
Security policy concept
A security policy is a rule or set of rules that defines how systems, users, or data should be protected.
security risks concept
Security risks are possible ways that systems, data, or people could be harmed by accidents, weaknesses, or attacks.
Security Stewardship Program organization
The Security Stewardship Program is a program that funds people who report security problems and maintainers who fix them.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.
Security Update concept
A software update that fixes vulnerabilities or other security-related problems.
security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.
Security Weakness concept
A flaw or unsafe condition that could allow unauthorized access, damage, or disruption.
self-hosted runners tool
Self-hosted runners are machines controlled by a user or company that run automated software build and deployment jobs.
Self-Service Provisioning concept
Self-service provisioning lets users create or configure computing resources themselves without waiting for a central IT team.
sender concept
A sender is the person, account, server, or system that sends a message such as an email.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
Serverless Functions concept
Serverless functions are small pieces of cloud-hosted code that run when needed without the owner managing a server.
service account concept
A non-human account used by an application or service to perform automated tasks, often holding elevated privileges.
service accounts concept
Service accounts are accounts used by software or systems rather than by individual people.

A Microsoft Entra identity representing an application or service so it can receive permissions and sign in programmatically.
Service principals concept
Service principals are non-human identities used by applications or services to access cloud resources.
also: second compromised service principal
session cookie concept
A session cookie is a small piece of browser data that keeps a user logged in while using a website.

session token concept
A session token is a temporary digital pass that keeps a user logged in after they authenticate.
severity scores concept
Severity scores rate how serious a vulnerability or security finding is.
SHA-256 concept
SHA-256 is a hashing method that creates a fixed-size digital fingerprint of data.
also: file's SHA-256 hash
SHA-256 hash concept
A SHA-256 hash is a fixed-length digital fingerprint used to identify data or files.
shadow-ai

Shadowserver organization
Shadowserver is an internet security watchdog group that tracks exposed systems and other security data.
shared credentials concept
Shared credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens used by more than one person or system.
sharepoint
SharePoint is Microsoft’s platform for storing, sharing, and collaborating on documents and internal websites.
shell tool
A shell is a command-line interface that lets a user or program run commands on a computer.
shell command concept
A text instruction given to a command-line interpreter to perform an operation, such as listing files or running a program.
shell commands concept
Shell commands are text instructions typed into a command line to tell a computer what to do.

A shell user is a system account used to run command-line instructions on a device.
also: Android's shell user
shellcode injection technique
Shellcode injection is putting small malicious code into another process so it runs inside that process.
shinyhunters

also: the prolific ShinyHunters hacking group, the group, the threat actor

Credentials that expire and are replaced automatically so a stolen credential works for only a limited time.

A security tool that gathers and analyzes logs from across an organization in real time to spot suspicious activity.
also: security information and event management (SIEM)
Significant Incident concept
A serious cybersecurity event that causes or could cause major harm, disruption, or risk.
Signing keys concept
Signing keys are cryptographic keys used to prove that software or data really came from a trusted publisher and was not changed.
Silent Push platform product
Silent Push platform is a threat intelligence platform used to investigate suspicious internet infrastructure such as domains and IP addresses.
silent-push organization
Silent Push is a threat intelligence company that tracks internet infrastructure used by attackers.
sim-swapping technique
SIM swapping is a fraud technique where criminals move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card they control.
Simulation concept
An imitation of a real-world situation used for testing, training, or study.
singapore
Singapore is a Southeast Asian country and technology hub often referenced in cybersecurity reporting.
Single Sign On concept
Single Sign On lets a person log in once and then access multiple approved apps without signing in again each time.
slack
Slack is a workplace messaging and collaboration platform.
SlowMist organization
A cybersecurity company that specializes in blockchain and cryptocurrency security investigations.

SMS is the standard text messaging service used on mobile phones.
Snowflake product
Snowflake is a cloud data platform used to store and analyze data.

SOAR, or security orchestration, automation, and response, is software that helps security teams automate investigations and response tasks.
also: security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR), SOAR integration
social engineering technique
Social engineering is manipulation of people into doing something or sharing information they otherwise would not.
social engineering lure technique
A social engineering lure is a message, story, or offer designed to trick a person into clicking, replying, paying, or sharing information.
Social engineering lures technique
Social engineering lures are tricks or messages designed to persuade people to click, download, or reveal information.
SOCRadar organization
SOCRadar is a cybersecurity company that provides threat intelligence and external attack surface monitoring services.

Software flaws are mistakes or weaknesses in programs that can cause bugs or create security risks.
software updates concept
Software updates are new versions or fixes released to improve features, repair bugs, or close security holes.

SOUL.md tool
A configuration file used to provide instructions or a persona to an AI agent.
source code concept
The human-readable code written by programmers that makes up software.
south-korea
South Korea is an East Asian country often referenced in cybersecurity stories involving technology, espionage, or regional threats.

Spearphishing is a targeted scam message sent to a specific person or group to trick them into giving access or information.
spearphishing-attachment technique

Spoof Transaction Data technique
To alter or fake transaction information so a system is misled about a payment or transfer.
spoofed technique
Spoofed means faked to look like it came from a trusted person, system, or address.

SQL injection is a web attack where malicious database commands are inserted into an application's input fields or requests.

A SQL injection flaw is a security weakness that can let an attacker send malicious database commands through an application's input fields.

A hacking tool used to repeatedly guess SSH login credentials until it finds a working combination.
SSH server tool
A service that accepts encrypted remote command-line connections through the Secure Shell protocol.
SSL Certificates protocol
SSL certificates are digital credentials that help websites prove their identity and encrypt connections with visitors.
standing-privileges

static analysis technique

stealer log concept

Stolen means taken without permission, such as stolen passwords, data, or devices.
stolen data concept
Stolen data is information taken without permission, often later sold, leaked, or used for extortion.
stolen information concept
Stolen information is data taken without permission, such as personal details, business files, passwords, or financial records.
stolen keys concept
Stolen keys are secret digital credentials, such as API keys or encryption keys, that attackers have taken and can use to access systems.

Storage Account Keys concept
Storage account keys are powerful secret credentials that can grant access to a cloud storage account.

Storage account-level deletion protection is a safeguard that prevents a cloud storage account from being deleted without extra authorization.

Storage Account-Level Protections concept
Storage account-level protections are security settings that help prevent unauthorized changes to a cloud storage account and its data.
Storage bucket concept
A storage bucket is a cloud folder-like container used to store files and data objects.
Storm-2570 threat-actor
Storm-2570 is a threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
Storm-2992 threat-actor
Storm-2992 is Microsoft's label for a threat-actor group tracked in security reporting.
Storm-3069 threat-actor
A temporary Microsoft name for a threat actor group associated with the use of NeedyMantis malware.
Storm-3168 threat-actor
Storm-3168 is Microsoft's name for the JadePuffer threat-actor group.
Strix tool
An open-source, self-hosted AI penetration-testing tool that can run with local models in isolated environments.
Student Records concept
Information an educational institution keeps about its students, such as enrollment, grades, or contact details.
also: student-record
subdomain concept
A subdomain is an extra part added before a main domain name, like blog.example.com.

also: take them over
Subdomains concept
Subdomains are parts of a domain name, such as blog.example.com, that can point to separate websites or services.
